shortcuts.command: powershell -NoProfile -Command "$sh = New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell; $dirs = @(\"$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\", \"$env:ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\", \"$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\", \"$env:PUBLIC\Desktop\"); Get-ChildItem -Path $dirs -Recurse -Filter *.lnk -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $s = $sh.CreateShortcut($_.FullName); [pscustomobject]@{ shortcut = $_.FullName; target = $s.TargetPath; args = $s.Arguments; workdir = $s.WorkingDirectory } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3 -Compress"

directories.command: powershell -NoProfile -Command "$roots = @(\"$env:ProgramFiles\", \"${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\", \"$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\", \"$env:LOCALAPPDATA\", \"$env:APPDATA\"); foreach ($root in $roots) { if (Test-Path $root) { Get-ChildItem -Path $root -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match 'watt|steam|beyond|toolkit' } | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName } } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress"

uninstall_entries.command: powershell -NoProfile -Command "$paths = @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*'); Get-ItemProperty -Path $paths -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -match 'watt|steam|beyond' } | Select-Object DisplayName,DisplayVersion,InstallLocation,DisplayIcon,UninstallString | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3 -Compress"

_doc: Standalone Watt Toolkit lifecycle test (handoff/TO_DSH.md). Scope limited to starting and stopping the local accelerator; no BuildReasonSeg model work. Read-only with respect to system configuration: DSH never edited the hosts file, the registry, the certificate store, PATH or the system proxy, and never force-killed a process. The hosts changes below were written by Watt Toolkit itself as its normal acceleration behaviour.

environment.desktop: interactive (explorer.exe present, Shell_TrayWnd reachable via UI Automation)

executable.distribution: Microsoft Store MSIX package (SignatureKind=Store); no Win32 shortcut exists
executable.found_via: Get-StartApps (display name 'Watt Toolkit') then Get-AppxPackage by PackageFamilyName
not_found_in: 187 Start Menu / Desktop shortcuts (no watt/steam++/beyond match)
C:/Program Files, C:/Program Files (x86), %LOCALAPPDATA%/Programs (no matching directory)

baseline_summary.mirrors_user_statement: Confirmed: at test start Watt Toolkit was exited and acceleration was off (0 Watt processes, 0 listeners on 443, 1 active hosts line with no relevant entries). huggingface.co did not resolve; GitHub/PyPI HTTPS worked.

startup.rationale: normal Start-Menu activation of the packaged app; no compatibility flags, no elevated mode, no undocumented switches
startup.application_window: appeared only after a second activation; class 'Avalonia-7b702aff-...'
startup.acceleration_evidence: within 20 s of launch the accelerator child process owned 0.0.0.0:443 and 0.0.0.0:80 and the hosts file gained a '# Steam++ Start' ... '# Steam++ End' block redirecting github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com and huggingface.co to 127.0.0.1

active_github_test.git_result: OK via git's schannel backend; HEAD 2b90b9f5ceec907a1c18123530e92e794ad901a4

URLError: <urlopen error [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1016)>

active_huggingface_test.improvement_over_baseline: yes: at baseline huggingface.co did not resolve at all; with acceleration on it resolves and returns real metadata through the OS trust store

tls_integrity.python_certifi_result_under_acceleration: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED 'unable to get local issuer certificate' for all four probes
tls_integrity.interpretation: Watt Toolkit intercepts TLS with its own root CA, which it installs into the Windows certificate store that git (schannel) and .NET/WinHTTP trust. The project's standard certifi bundle does not trust it. Per TO_DSH section 6 this is recorded as a limitation; the old cert-injection workaround was NOT reintroduced.

method_attempted.purpose: make a normal window close possible

method_attempted.action: read-only UI Automation survey of that window and of the desktop tree
method_attempted.result: UIAutomationClient loaded, but the app window exposes 0 descendants and 0 named controls, so no control could be invoked by name and no in-app navigation was possible without blind coordinate clicking (forbidden)

method_attempted.action: Get-Process -Id 21808 | CloseMainWindow()   # == WM_CLOSE, the same request as the title-bar X
method_attempted.result: returned True but only minimized to tray: all three processes still running, :443/:80 still listening, hosts block unchanged after 15 s

no force-kill was used; Stop-Process -Force and taskkill /F were never invoked, and no helper process was terminated

not_attempted_because_forbidden_or_unsaf: terminating the accelerator helper process (explicitly forbidden)
blind coordinate clicking inside the app window or the tray menu
editing the hosts file to undo Watt's block
editing app settings or the registry

post_shutdown_verification.reason: no graceful stop or exit mechanism was available, so no post-shutdown state exists

classification.definition: DSH can reliably start Watt Toolkit and acceleration starts automatically with it, but DSH cannot safely stop acceleration or exit the application.
classification.secondary_explanation: TO_DSH section 10 defines FAILED_UNSAFE_STATE as the test leaving a network/proxy state different from baseline that DSH cannot restore safely. That condition currently holds: the hosts file carries Watt's 211-line block, Steam++.Accelerator.exe owns :443/:80, and DSH cannot restore baseline. It is reported as a secondary condition rather than the primary classification because nothing is broken or misconfigured -- it is the expected consequence of a start-only automation and the user can restore baseline in two clicks.
classification.future_workflow: DSH starts Watt Toolkit; acceleration comes up automatically; after the networked work the user manually stops acceleration and exits Watt Toolkit from its tray icon.

user_interaction_required.action: Open the Watt Toolkit tray icon (hidden-icons area of the taskbar -> the icon named 'Watt Toolkit'), use '停止加速' / turn acceleration off, then choose '退出' (Exit). Do NOT rely on the window X: it only minimizes to tray.
user_interaction_required.how_to_verify: Afterwards there should be 0 processes named Steam++.exe / Steam++.Accelerator.exe, nothing listening on :443 or :80, and the hosts file back to 1 active line (sha256 b42f2099187886def637d6aa840022266e05cb6c987a9394e708e23cd505eb46).
user_interaction_required.for_future_runs: Watt must be stopped manually; DSH cannot automate the stop side on this version.

safety_warnings: The machine is currently NOT at its pre-test baseline: Watt Toolkit's hosts block and its local :443/:80 listeners are active.

Watt Toolkit intercepts TLS with its own root CA. Python's standard certifi bundle does not trust it, so python/urllib/httpx/requests will fail certificate verification while acceleration is on. Do not fix this by injecting certificates into certifi.
git and .NET/WinHTTP work while acceleration is on because they use the Windows trust store.
No force-kill, hosts edit, registry edit, certificate change or proxy change was performed by DSH.
limitations: GUI control automation is not possible: the app is an Avalonia build whose windows expose no UI Automation tree, and its tray context menu is not UIA-readable.
No documented CLI shutdown switch exists for this version and none was guessed.
DSH cannot verify the post-shutdown state until the user stops Watt manually.
